title: The Sum of the Two Smallest Numbers in a Range

concept.title: A node stores its two smallest numbers; merging two nodes keeps the two smallest of the four
body: A row of numbers changes one cell at a time. A question gives a range of **at least two** cells and asks for the **sum of the two smallest numbers** in it (two cells, so equal values count twice). For `4 1 7 1 9` the two smallest of the cells 1 to 5 are 1 and 1, with the sum 2; of the cells 1 to 3 they are 1 and 4, with the sum 5. Sorting the range for each question costs O(n log n).

The tree needs a merge rule for a pair `(m1, m2)`, the smallest and the second smallest value of the block (use infinity if the block has only one cell). To merge two blocks, take the four numbers `m1, m2, m1', m2'` and keep the two smallest. The neutral node is `(inf, inf)`. A leaf is `(value, inf)`. Because the "two smallest of the union" does not depend on how the blocks are grouped, the rule is associative, and the usual tree loops work.

body.code:
def merge(p, q):                       # p and q are pairs (smallest, second smallest)
    a, b = p
    c, d = q
    if c < a: a, b, c, d = c, d, a, b # now a is the smaller first element
    # the two smallest are a and min(b, c)
    return (a, min(b, c))

answer = res[0] + res[1]

body: After the swap the first number of the result is `a` (the global minimum) and the second is the smaller of `b` (the second of the same block) and `c` (the minimum of the other block): `d` can never be among the two smallest. Each merge is a few comparisons, so the cost is O(log n) per operation. The same pair idea gives the second maximum and the "smallest and its count" nodes.

statement: A row of `n` numbers is given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `x y` sets the number at the position `x` to `y`; type 2 `x y` (with `x < y`) asks for the sum of the two smallest numbers among the positions `x` to `y` (two different cells; equal values both count). Print the answers to the questions on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of cells and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the cells.

Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `x` and `y`. If `t = 1`, set the cell number `x` to the value `y`. If `t = 2`, print the sum of the two smallest numbers among the cells `x` to `y` (here `x < y`).
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.
constraints: For a question 1 <= x < y <= n.

examples.note: The two smallest of the whole row are 1 and 1: 2. Of the cells 1..3 they are 1 and 4: 5. The output is 2 5.

hints: Store (smallest, second smallest) in each node.
Merging two nodes: the smallest of the four values and the next smallest.
The neutral node holds two infinities.

solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).
